newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEMBLEY ON SECURITY ALERT FOR LEAGUE CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEMBLEY ON SECURITY ALERT FOR LEAGUE CUP FINAL.

text.p: Police warned fans attending Sunday's English League Cup final at Wembley Stadium to be "extra vigilant" following the incidents that led to the abandonment of the Grand National on Saturday.
Around 75,000 fans are expected at the stadium for the final between Leicester City and Middlesbrough which is due to be shown live to 60 countries around the world.
A Scotland Yard spokesman told Reuters: "Of course we cannot discuss sensitive areas of security, but we are satisfied that the policing arrangements we have in hand will cater for any contingency.
"Our advice to fans is to be extra vigilant, the same sort of advice we give to anyone in London in the current climate of possible terrorist activity."
Extra police are likely to be drafted in to patrol the match in north London with even tighter controls than usual on traffic, personal searches and ticketing.

A Wembley spokesman said: "Wembley is a high profile venue and we have had a high level of security in operation for many years now. We have an obligation to protect players and fans. The stadium and grounds are combed before every match and we are hopeful that this afternoon's match will go ahead without a problem.
Wembley have urged fans to arrive at the stadium as early as possible and to travel by public transport

Adrian Titcombe, the head of security for the Football Association said: "It is the task of the Wembley stewards to make sure the stadium is secure and they will mount a routine search before the game to make sure the stadium is safe for the public to enter.

"Unfortunately, security alerts at football grounds are not new. You always get calls before games warning of bombs or something similar. Most turn out to be hoaxes but they still have to be checked."

The match is scheduled to kickoff at 3pm (1400 gmt) with the pre-match entertainment beginning 90 minutes earlier. Unlike the F.A. Cup Final in May, which is often attended by a senior member of the Royal Family, no senior royal is attending Sunday's match.
